content: Methyl orange is a pH indicator that is commonly utilized in titration procedures. It is frequently selected for use in titrations due to its distinct and easily observable color change. This indicator undergoes a color transition at the pH of a moderately strong acid, making it particularly suitable for titrations involving acids. Unlike a universal indicator, methyl orange does not exhibit a full spectrum of color changes but instead provides a more precise and well-defined endpoint. In solutions that are becoming less acidic, methyl orange transitions from red to orange and eventually to yellow. Conversely, in solutions that are increasing in acidity, the color change occurs in the reverse order. It is important to note that the entire color change process takes place under acidic conditions. Specifically, methyl orange appears reddish in acidic environments and yellow in alkaline conditions. A modified version of methyl orange, known as screened methyl orange, is a solution composed of methyl orange and xylene cyanol. This modified indicator changes color from gray to green as the solution becomes more basic. Additionally, a variety of other commonly used pH indicators are listed and described in the article on pH indicators.
